factors.name: Size and parallel branching
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.92–0.97) of Size, Token split, Control flow complexity, Number of empty sequence flows and Coefficient of network connectivity, plus Maximum connector degree (0.80) and a moderate Connector Mismatch (0.56), describe nets that are larger and contain more splits, especially parallel ones, and more arcs per node. Density loads negatively (-0.43, not assigned), consistent with density falling as nets grow. With about 50% of the variance it is the dominant dimension.

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.90) and Density (0.81) load highly, so this factor captures how many arcs connectors have relative to net size, largely independent of absolute size. Connector Heterogeneity loads negatively (-0.49), so nets with denser, high-degree connectors tend to use mostly one connector type. Maximum connector degree also loads moderately (0.41) next to its main loading on Factor 1.

factors.name: Sequential, separable structure
factors.summary: Separability (0.93) and Sequentiality (0.76) load highly, describing nets with many articulation points and many arcs between non-connector nodes, i.e. chain-like, sequential structure. It rests on two measures, though both are clear and conceptually related.

factors.name: Connector type mix (weak)
factors.summary: Only Connector Heterogeneity loads notably (0.62), and it cross-loads on Factor 2 (-0.49). The factor explains just 4.4% of the variance and its eigenvalue (0.68) is below 1, so it is essentially a single-measure factor.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, overall KMO 0.83). Four varimax factors explain 86% of the variance, dominated by a size and parallel branching factor (50%), followed by connector degree/density (17%) and sequential, separable structure (15%). A fourth, weak factor is carried by Connector Heterogeneity alone. Three factors were suggested and three eigenvalues exceed 1, so the four-factor solution likely over-extracts. All measures are assigned; Connector Mismatch has a low communality (0.37).
caveats: Four factors were extracted although three were suggested, so Factor 4 rests on one measure with an eigenvalue below 1 and may not be a stable dimension.
Connector Heterogeneity cross-loads on Factors 4 and 2, and its MSA (0.61) is close to the threshold.
Average connector degree and Density, which define Factor 2, have MSA values only slightly above 0.6.
Connector Mismatch is only moderately explained (communality 0.37), so its assignment to Factor 1 is weak.
Number of duplicate tasks was removed as constant, so duplicate or silent labels play no role in this solution.
The factors reflect shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and depend on the discovery algorithms, the rotation and the number of factors.
